A layer is a block of operators that a model composes, such as a dense layer with its activation. The language has no `layer` construct yet, and a model function is the unit of composition, inlined into the Tensor IR (DESIGN.md § 0, invariant 2; § 2.1). So each entry below is a small model whose `forward` is the block, checked by `modelspec check`, and its diagram is the model view of that program: the nodes its prediction reaches, without the loss and the target.

Each diagram shows the block expanded: an `Input` per argument of `forward`, one box per operator, and each parameter with one reader drawn as a chip on that reader. Drawing the block collapsed, as one function composite that zooms into this level, arrives with zoom (DESIGN.md § 13.3).

## Dense

A linear layer without bias: one `matmul` of the input by a weight.

[`crates/modelspec-docs/models/layers/dense.mspec`](https://github.com/beyond10x/modelspec/blob/main/crates/modelspec-docs/models/layers/dense.mspec):

```modelspec title="crates/modelspec-docs/models/layers/dense.mspec"
model Dense {
    param w: Tensor<f32, [4, 8]> = xavier_uniform();

    fn forward(x: Tensor<f32, [16, 4]>)
        -> Tensor<f32, [16, 8]> {
        return matmul(x, w);
    }
}

train FitDense {
    model = Dense;
    input x: Tensor<f32, [16, 4]>;
    target y: Tensor<f32, [16, 8]>;
    loss = mse(model.forward(x), y);
    optimizer = sgd(lr = 0.05);
    steps = 100;
    seed = 7;
    device = cpu;
}
```

## Dense with relu

The dense layer followed by its activation, `relu(matmul(x, w))`.

[`crates/modelspec-docs/models/layers/dense_relu.mspec`](https://github.com/beyond10x/modelspec/blob/main/crates/modelspec-docs/models/layers/dense_relu.mspec):

```modelspec title="crates/modelspec-docs/models/layers/dense_relu.mspec"
model DenseRelu {
    param w: Tensor<f32, [4, 8]> = xavier_uniform();

    fn forward(x: Tensor<f32, [16, 4]>)
        -> Tensor<f32, [16, 8]> {
        return relu(matmul(x, w));
    }
}

train FitDenseRelu {
    model = DenseRelu;
    input x: Tensor<f32, [16, 4]>;
    target y: Tensor<f32, [16, 8]>;
    loss = mse(model.forward(x), y);
    optimizer = sgd(lr = 0.05);
    steps = 100;
    seed = 7;
    device = cpu;
}
```

<ModelDiagram data={layerDenseRelu} view="model" />

## Dense with bias and gelu

The feed-forward half of a transformer layer: `add_rows` adds the bias `b` to every row of the product, then `gelu`.

[`crates/modelspec-docs/models/layers/dense_bias_gelu.mspec`](https://github.com/beyond10x/modelspec/blob/main/crates/modelspec-docs/models/layers/dense_bias_gelu.mspec):

```modelspec title="crates/modelspec-docs/models/layers/dense_bias_gelu.mspec"
model DenseBiasGelu {
    param w: Tensor<f32, [4, 8]> = xavier_uniform();
    param b: Tensor<f32, [8]> = zeros();

    fn forward(x: Tensor<f32, [16, 4]>)
        -> Tensor<f32, [16, 8]> {
        return gelu(add_rows(matmul(x, w), b));
    }
}

train FitDenseBiasGelu {
    model = DenseBiasGelu;
    input x: Tensor<f32, [16, 4]>;
    target y: Tensor<f32, [16, 8]>;
    loss = mse(model.forward(x), y);
    optimizer = sgd(lr = 0.05);
    steps = 100;
    seed = 7;
    device = cpu;
}
```

<ModelDiagram data={layerDenseBiasGelu} view="model" />

## Residual and layer norm

A post-layer-norm residual: the sublayer `f` is added back to its input and the sum normalised, `layer_norm(add(x, f), gamma, beta)`.

[`crates/modelspec-docs/models/layers/layer_norm_residual.mspec`](https://github.com/beyond10x/modelspec/blob/main/crates/modelspec-docs/models/layers/layer_norm_residual.mspec):

```modelspec title="crates/modelspec-docs/models/layers/layer_norm_residual.mspec"
model LayerNormResidual {
    param w: Tensor<f32, [8, 8]> = xavier_uniform();
    param gamma: Tensor<f32, [8]> = ones();
    param beta: Tensor<f32, [8]> = zeros();

    fn forward(x: Tensor<f32, [16, 8]>)
        -> Tensor<f32, [16, 8]> {
        let f = matmul(x, w);
        return layer_norm(add(x, f), gamma, beta);
    }
}

train FitLayerNormResidual {
    model = LayerNormResidual;
    input x: Tensor<f32, [16, 8]>;
    target y: Tensor<f32, [16, 8]>;
    loss = mse(model.forward(x), y);
    optimizer = sgd(lr = 0.05);
    steps = 100;
    seed = 7;
    device = cpu;
}
```

<ModelDiagram data={layerLayerNormResidual} view="model" />

## Self-attention

Three projections of one input, the queries, keys and values, read by one `attention` with two heads and a key mask.

[`crates/modelspec-docs/models/layers/self_attention.mspec`](https://github.com/beyond10x/modelspec/blob/main/crates/modelspec-docs/models/layers/self_attention.mspec):

```modelspec title="crates/modelspec-docs/models/layers/self_attention.mspec"
model SelfAttention {
    param wq: Tensor<f32, [8, 8]> = xavier_uniform();
    param wk: Tensor<f32, [8, 8]> = xavier_uniform();
    param wv: Tensor<f32, [8, 8]> = xavier_uniform();

    fn forward(x: Tensor<f32, [16, 8]>, key_mask: Tensor<f32, [2, 8]>)
        -> Tensor<f32, [16, 8]> {
        let q = matmul(x, wq);
        let k = matmul(x, wk);
        let v = matmul(x, wv);
        return attention(q, k, v, key_mask, heads = 2);
    }
}

train FitSelfAttention {
    model = SelfAttention;
    input x: Tensor<f32, [16, 8]>;
    input key_mask: Tensor<f32, [2, 8]>;
    target y: Tensor<f32, [16, 8]>;
    loss = mse(model.forward(x, key_mask), y);
    optimizer = sgd(lr = 0.05);
    steps = 100;
    seed = 7;
    device = cpu;
}
```
